sections.overview: Mullus barbatus is a pink goatfish of the eastern Atlantic and Mediterranean; compare the striped red mullet, Mullus surmuletus, in its profile.
sections.identification: It has a steep head profile, two barbels beneath the mouth and no conspicuous stripes, unlike the striped Mullus surmuletus.
sections.habitat: It is demersal over shelf bottoms of mud, sand or gravel; the Adriatic species account reports mainly muddy habitat at about 5–250 m.
sections.diet: It feeds on small bottom-dwelling crustaceans, worms and molluscs.
sections.behavior: In parts of the Adriatic, juveniles move offshore and adults make seasonal movements toward spawning areas; the pattern varies by locality.
sections.reproduction: The FAO AdriaMed account reports Adriatic spawning in late spring and summer, with females spawning from April to May in the cited studies.
sections.ecology: It searches the seabed for prey with sensory chin barbels, which it shares with Mullus surmuletus.
sections.conservation: It is commercially important in the Mediterranean; FishBase lists an IUCN field linked to the 2025-2 global assessment, but I did not verify the category.
